newsitem.title: FINLAND: Kemira says Pigments unit had 1996 loss.
newsitem.headline: Kemira says Pigments unit had 1996 loss.

text.p: Finnish chemicals group Kemira Oy said in a statement on Tuesday that its Kemira Pigments unit had made an operating loss in 1996.
"The operating result of the Kemira Pigments group for 1996 will be significantly worse than the previous year (a 255 million markka operating profit) and in the red," Kemira said.
"The market outlook for 1997 is slightly better than in 1996. Planned titanium dioxide price hikes will, however, not significantly improve thew profitability of the Kemira Pigments group," it said.
Profitability at Kemira Pigments' Pori plant in south-western Finland had been "developing weakly in 1996 and the situation is expected to remain difficult this year as well," Kemira said.
It announced measures aiming at reducing the Pori plant's 960-strong workforce by about 200 people. "The target is annual savings of 100 million markka from 1999 onward," it said.
